newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW-BANK OF ENGLAND INFLATION REPORT.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW-BANK OF ENGLAND INFLATION REPORT.

text.p: Following is a selection of analysts' comments on the release of the Bank of England's quarterly inflation report:
"The main point is they still see some inflation risk. Our interpretation is that rates are on hold for now, but we haven't seen the peak."

"Reading the headlines, there seem very few surprises. It merely amplifies the key statement after last week's interest rate decision. But clearly they are warning that interest rates will have to rise in future either if growth doesn't slow as much as they hoped or because average earnings growth picks up."

"The Bank of England is confirming what they said last week, that they're on hold for the time being. But recent inflation is on the upside, which is certainly our view. It is quite clear that we will have a pause where they will assess the data, and as a result it will tip them into another rate rise in November."
DON EGGINGTON, DAIWA INSTITUTE OF RESEARCH

"It was what we were expecting. Their view is consistent with city economists. Growth is too rapid and needs to be slowed. The peak in interest rates is still contingent on the exchange rate. If sterling remains at current levels then seven percent is probably the peak."
"The key point (the Bank of England) made when they raised interest rates after the last meeting was that a peak had been reached. The market knows now that interest rates have not reached a peak.
"I see a further 50 basis point rise in two stages. They are concerned about money supply and concerned about rising wages. I don't think sterling will fall out of bed, but it is the greatest risk."
